claims.claim: Generator fidelity orders how much red-teaming DEGRADES real-fraud recall: the higher-fidelity generator costs about a third as much recall, in every seed.
claims.derivation: Recall on held-out real fraud per arm minus the A0 baseline, at an FPR pinned to 1% on a disjoint legitimate validation split.
claims.boundary: Both deltas are NEGATIVE: the A0 baseline is already at a ceiling (~0.999 recall), so the SIGN of transfer is not testable on this corpus -- only the ordering of harm. Three seeds; synthetic environment fraud; fixed augmentation budget.

claims.claim: The independent-marginal generator is trivially distinguishable from real fraud.
claims.derivation: Cross-validated ROC-AUC of a random forest separating real from synthetic rows.
claims.boundary: Measured against held-out real fraud, never the generator's fit slice.

claims.claim: Operating thresholds are calibrated without leakage.
claims.derivation: Threshold pinned at 1% FPR on a legitimate validation split, then measured on a disjoint test split.
claims.boundary: Temporal split; non-stationarity beyond the corpus window is untested.

claims.claim: Precision degrades sharply at production base rate.
claims.derivation: Bayes adjustment p*R / (p*R + (1-p)*FPR) applied to the measured operating point.
claims.boundary: Prevalence is a deployment assumption, not a measurement.

claims.claim: False positives dominate the cost ledger at a 1% false-positive rate.
claims.derivation: Insult cost per false positive = lost margin + support contact + churn probability * CLV.
claims.boundary: INR rates are stated order-of-magnitude assumptions and are overridable.

claims.claim: An ungated closed loop raises recall on its own synthetic attacks while LOWERING recall on held-out real fraud.
claims.derivation: V0 vs final-generation recall on two disjoint yardsticks at an FPR pinned to 1% on a disjoint legitimate validation split.
claims.boundary: Simulated ring fraud; three seeds; fixed attack budget per generation.

claims.claim: A label-free fidelity gate protects real-fraud recall by rejecting low-fidelity escape batches before retraining.
claims.derivation: Gated arm delta-real-recall minus ungated arm delta-real-recall, identical attacker, budget and detector.
claims.boundary: Gate thresholds fixed in advance (C2ST <= 0.90, rank-dependence <= 1.50), never tuned per seed.

claims.claim: The gate needs no fraud labels and is computable before any retraining occurs.
claims.derivation: C2ST AUC and Spearman rank-correlation Frobenius distance between the escape batch and the real fraud rows already in training.
claims.boundary: Requires >= 20 escapes to measure; smaller batches are refused by default.

claims.claim: All 8 attack families are executable and individually measured, not merely listed.
claims.derivation: Per-family non-APPROVE rate on a fresh evaluation corpus at a pinned operating point.
claims.boundary: Synthetic environment; each family generated through the same Plausibility Gate as every other payload.

claims.claim: Families withheld from supervised training are still detected by the unsupervised and graph layers.
claims.derivation: Leave-one-family-out: the measured family is absent from supervised training; recall and per-layer attribution reported.
claims.boundary: The unsupervised layers see legitimate traffic only, so this measures architecture rather than memorisation.

claims.claim: The full four-layer decision stack scores inline at p99 15.15 ms, inside a 100 ms authorisation budget.
claims.derivation: time.perf_counter() around DecisionEngine.decide() over a mixed legit/attack stream, warmup excluded.
claims.boundary: Single-threaded on one machine; excludes network transport and ISO message parsing.

claims.claim: All 14 attack families are executable and individually measured, not merely listed.
claims.derivation: Per-family non-APPROVE rate on a fresh evaluation corpus at a pinned operating point.
claims.boundary: Synthetic environment; each family generated through the same Plausibility Gate as every other payload.

claims.claim: All 14 attack families are executable and individually measured, not merely listed.
claims.derivation: Per-family non-APPROVE rate on a fresh evaluation corpus, at a full-stack operating point calibrated on a mixed split disjoint from training and evaluation and re-pinned for every seed and withheld family.
claims.boundary: Synthetic environment; each family generated through the same Plausibility Gate as every other payload.

claims.claim: Families withheld from supervised training are still detected by the unsupervised and graph layers.
claims.derivation: Leave-one-family-out: the measured family is absent from supervised training; recall and per-layer attribution reported.
claims.boundary: The unsupervised layers see legitimate traffic only, so this measures architecture rather than memorisation.
